Hi Sarah — appreciate the clear list. We can get these across today/tomorrow. Summary below and see attachments for the artifacts: redwood_dpa_annex_v2.pdf and an annotated dataflow diagram.

- Subprocessors: attached roster in the DPA annex (AppSec + Legal approved list). Subprocessors that process raw PII are called out in section 2.2 with country locations. Short summary: primary infra providers (AWS US regions), analytics/telemetry (Redwood-owned telemetry service, US/EU staging), model-hosting partners (dedicated pools may be in EU for regional deployments on request).

- Dataflow: attached redwood_annotated_dataflow_v3.png shows boundaries for tokenization, prefix/KV cache (ephemeral), long-term logs (retention window), and export paths. PHI/PII are marked. Default hosted option keeps customer data in the chosen region; cross-border transfers are by default to the US unless customer opts for EU-only Dedicated/Private — we call that out as a configuration and can provide residency guarantees for Dedicated/Private deployments.

- KMS custody: short answer: we support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated (by default customer-managed KMS). For Hosted customers we provide a KeyProxy model where keys are rotated by the customer and proxied; the KMS custody statement (kms_key_custody_statement.pdf) is attached. We don’t hold plaintext keys. For cases requiring HSM attestation, we can coordinate an HSM export audit or provide third-party attestation artifacts.

Next steps: I’ve attached the DPA annex with the subprocessor roster called out. If you need priority evidence (e.g., signed attestation), let me know and I’ll escalate to Marissa and our security ops team.

Hi Sarah — Marissa from Privacy & Compliance here. Quick technical clarifications to accompany Vivek's notes:

- Tokenization & minimization: our ingest layer performs deterministic tokenization for configured fields; the annotated diagram indicates which fields we tokenize vs store verbatim. For PHI we recommend the Dedicated/Private flows; for Hosted we apply minimization and strict retention.

- Access controls: role-based access with separation of duties; operational engineers do not have decryption rights for customer-managed keys. Access to logs containing PII is restricted and audited via IAM + our internal privileged-access tooling.

- Cross-border justification: non-US subprocessors are limited; transfers happen only for operational reasons (e.g., failover) unless the customer explicitly requests multi-region. The DPA annex includes language for data transfer mechanisms and SCCs where needed.

- Evidence we can provide immediately: exported subprocessor CSV with country columns (included in the annex), the annotated dataflow (PNG), and our KMS custody statement (PDF). For cryptographic attestation (HSM), we need a week to coordinate with the infra partner to produce an HSM attestation copy. If MedGrove needs this sooner we can prioritize.

If you want us to produce a short two-page summary that your legal team can attach to the DPA, I can draft that and include a proposed redline for section 6 (cross-border transfers).

- Marissa
Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference
